text: The Thessaly Weir diverts the Callan, according to a memorandum released Tuesday by the Ministry of Works and reviewed by The Continental Record. The document says the structure, completed in 2019 near the town of Brackenford, channels an average of 38 million liters a day into the East Marsh irrigation network. Deputy minister Elian Voss said the diversion was designed to stabilize summer water levels downstream while preserving flood capacity during winter rains. The ministry’s hydrology annex, dated March 4, notes that the weir’s sluice gates were recalibrated in January after a dry-season drop of 11 percent on the Callan. Local councils welcomed the change, citing improved allocations for farms and mills.
